subject: science
passage: Concrete cracks. Fissures open as the material shrinks and shifts, and once water seeps in, it corrodes the steel inside, so that repair bills for bridges mount for decades. Researchers in the Netherlands have proposed letting concrete heal itself. They mix into the wet concrete small capsules containing dormant bacterial spores and a food source, calcium lactate. <u>The spores can survive for years inside the hardened material, inactive until a crack forms and water reaches them.</u> Then the bacteria wake, consume the lactate, and excrete limestone, which fills the crack within weeks. Tests show that cracks up to a millimeter wide can be sealed this way, though the capsules add considerably to the cost, and the approach has so far been used mainly in small structures.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains how the limestone produced by the bacteria seals the cracks.
choices.B: It describes the property of the spores that allows the repair mechanism to remain available until it is needed.
choices.C: It presents evidence that the method works in structures of any size.
choices.D: It identifies a drawback of the method that the final sentence then addresses.

explanation.why: The underlined sentence comes right after the capsules are introduced and right before the healing process is described. It explains that the spores stay dormant for years and become active only when a crack lets water in. That property is what makes the repair available exactly when it is needed, which the next sentence ("Then the bacteria wake") builds on.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The limestone and the sealing are described in the sentence that follows, not in the underlined one.
explanation.B: Correct. Dormancy for years, ended only by a crack and water, is the feature that lets the bacteria act at the right moment.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sentence offers no test evidence, and the text later says the method has been used "mainly in small structures."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Long survival of the spores is an advantage, not a drawback; the drawbacks (cost, limited use) appear only in the final sentence.
